question: When should you stop fly fishing for trout in the Smoky Mountains?
answer: Stop fishing for trout when water temperatures reach 65°F — and absolutely stop at 70°F. Trout caught in 70°F+ water have a very slim chance of survival even when carefully released. July and August are the off-season for trout fishing in Western North Carolina. Guides and outfitters who book summer trout trips regardless of water temperature are profiteers — not stewards of the resource. Check the live water temperature widget at macbrownflyfish.com before heading out.

question: What should fly fishers target in summer when trout streams are too warm?
answer: Smallmouth bass, carp, perch, and bluegill in the warmer river systems of Western North Carolina — the Little Tennessee River in particular. These species thrive in summer water temperatures and provide excellent fly fishing action with similar techniques to trout fishing. Chub on the wild streams of Great Smoky Mountains National Park also provide a great opportunity to practice nymphing techniques through the middle of the day. Mac Brown offers warm water guided trips during summer.

question: How do I choose an ethical fly fishing guide in North Carolina?
answer: Ask the guide directly: do you fish for trout when water temperatures exceed 65°F? Any guide who answers yes — or who books summer trout trips without checking water temperatures — is not a steward of the resource. Also ask about their qualifications, teaching ability, and whether the trip includes genuine instruction. Price alone is not a reliable indicator — guides in the Smoky Mountains range from $40 to over $500 for the same water. Look for certified instructors with verifiable credentials.

question: Is excessive fishing pressure damaging trout streams in the Smoky Mountains?
answer: Yes — and it is an increasing problem on delayed harvest streams due to the growing number of new fly fishers, guides, and outfitters. A delayed harvest stream requires only 30 feet of space between anglers — but the sheer volume of pressure concentrates fish and makes them increasingly selective over time. Wild streams require a mile or more of separation for a quality experience. Learn to read secondary water and fish away from crowds.

question: Why does Mac Brown not fish for trout in July and August?
answer: Because it is the ethical decision for the resource. Trout caught in water above 70°F face severely elevated mortality even with careful catch and release. Mac Brown Fly Fish switches to warm water species during the height of summer — targeting smallmouth bass and carp — and returns to trout guiding when water temperatures drop back into the productive range in September. This is not a business decision. It is a conservation decision.
